The function $p(x)$ is defined and differentiable on $[-5,3].$ The graph of ${p}^{′}(x)$, the derivative of $p(x),$ is shown above, where the area of the region between the graph and the $x$-axis is $9.$

Given that $p(3)=-4,$ what is the maximum value ${p}_{\text{max}}$ of $p(x)$ on the interval $[-5,3]?$

${p}_{\text{max}}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
According to the candidates' test, the maximum value of $p(x)$ on $[-5,3]$ must occur at a critical point or an endpoint of the interval.

**Step 1**: Find the critical points:

We see that ${p}^{′}(x)$ is defined everywhere on $x\in (-5,3),$ and ${p}^{′}(x)\ne 0$ inside the interval. Therefore, the candidates are $x=-5,3.$

**Step 2**: Compute the value of $p$ for each candidate using the fundamental theorem of calculus:

Using the given information and the fundamental theorem of calculus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}p(3) & =-4 \\ p(-5) & =p(3)+{\int }_{3}^{-5}{p}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =p(3)-{\int }_{-5}^{3}{p}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-4-9 \\  & =-13\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Select the largest value of $p$ from our candidates.

Comparing the values of $p$ found in step $2,$ we have

$$
{p}_{\text{max}}=max\{-4,-13\}=-4.
$$

Therefore, the maximum value of $p$ is ${p}_{\text{max}}=-4,$ and the value of $x$ that maximizes $p(x)$ is ${x}_{\text{max}}=3.$
